note: Strengths and risks for each approach. Entry counts may differ; tools/approach_pages.py enforces prose budgets within and across approaches. Scenario figures remain on the scenario page. BUILD-LOG.md records the basis for each entry. Where present, schema_evidence identifies checked schema fragments and is not rendered.

catalog-first.intro: Publishing technical hardening guidance as a catalog has these strengths and risks.

pros.title: Technical and regulatory requirements use one model
pros.body: Technical requirements use catalog controls and follow the same references through the remaining OSCAL models as regulatory controls.

pros.title: Rules can be tailored
pros.body: A profile selects the hardening requirements an organisation adopts and sets organisationally defined parameters without changing the source catalog.

pros.title: Catalog structures represent guide content
pros.body: Controls, parts and nested groups represent checks, remediation and explanatory prose, including the structure of a thousand-page guide.

pros.title: Third parties can publish framework mappings
pros.body: A separate mapping-collection links guidance to a framework, allowing a third party to publish the mapping without owning either catalog.

cons.title: Benchmark catalogs add maintenance work
cons.body: The system security plan must address benchmark requirements alongside regulatory controls; whether each additional catalog requires a separate plan remains unsettled.

cons.title: Combined baselines complicate profile resolution
cons.body: Multiple frameworks and benchmarks require catalogs, profiles and mappings to be maintained together, increasing tool integration work and profile resolution complexity.

cons.title: Responses do not identify individual instances
cons.body: A by-component response identifies a component, not an instance, so one exception among a hundred hosts sharing that component cannot be distinguished.

component-first.intro: Publishing technical hardening rules in a component definition has these strengths and risks.

pros.title: One artifact describes capability and supports automation
pros.body: A component definition describes how a product can meet controls; the proposed rules provide configuration requirements for automation in the same document.

pros.title: Rules and checks remain separate
pros.body: The product component holds the rule and a validation component holds the check; a second engine uses a second validation component.

pros.title: Implementation claims can reference rules
pros.body: The proposed implementing-rules assembly links a control implementation claim to the rule used to satisfy the control.

pros.title: Technology providers can extend component descriptions
pros.body: Existing guidance directs technology providers to describe product capabilities in component definitions, where the proposal would also place hardening rules.

cons.title: Four models require schema changes
cons.body: The proposal changes component definitions, system security plans, assessment plans and assessment results; existing schema support does not cover the proposed assemblies.

cons.title: Desired state enters the plan of record
cons.body: Rules describing the required component configuration enter the system security plan, which documents the system's implemented controls and current configuration.

cons.title: Published rules omit guide context
cons.body: Rationale, audit procedure and remediation provide guidance context, but the published rules omit these fields and support remains proposed.

cons.title: Responses do not identify individual instances
cons.body: A by-component response can reference a rule but not an individual instance, so exceptions remain associated with the component.

cons.title: Host-level claims may require inventory support
cons.body: Inventory items would also need implementing-rules support for a claim to identify a host rather than a component class.

assessment-first.intro: Publishing technical hardening guidance as an assessment plan has these strengths and risks.

pros.title: Guidance stays outside the plan of record
pros.body: The assessment plan references implementation claims without adding claims, so adding or retiring a guide does not change the system security plan.

pros.title: Assessment results reference an assessment plan
pros.body: A separate assessment results document imports a plan; the corpus includes findings that target objectives and reference supporting observations.

pros.title: Subjects can identify individual hosts
pros.body: An assessment subject can be an inventory item, allowing separate findings for two hosts running one operating system with different configurations.

pros.title: The plan records execution context
pros.body: Tasks carry schedules and identify execution platforms, placing the timing and runtime context for checks in the assessment plan.

cons.title: Required values lack resolvable parameters
cons.body: The activity title contains the required value, so changing the value requires editing the plan rather than resolving a profile.

cons.title: Guide hierarchy is limited to two tiers
cons.body: The model provides activities and steps, so guidance nested four levels deep must be represented within those two structural tiers.

cons.title: Published references and types need correction
cons.body: The published result references a plan absent from the corpus and assigns an observation a subject type not defined by the model.
